title: Vetala Story 24: The Prince and the Princess Who Could Not Be Separated
summary: The Vetala said: 'Hearken, King, to the lovers who conquered exile!'...
keywords: vetala story 24: the prince and the princess who could not be separated
full_text:
King Vikramaditya recaptured the corpse and hauled it across his shoulders.

The Vetala said: 'Hearken, King, to the lovers who conquered exile!'

A prince and princess were shipwrecked on opposite sides of an ocean. For ten years, each believed the other dead, yet each refused to wed another, living as ascetics in the forest.

When they reunited at an ancient temple, their hair was gray, but their love shone as bright as dawn.

The Vetala asked: 'King Vikramaditya, which preserved their love through ten years of silence?'

Vikramaditya replied: 'Their unshakeable faith in each other's virtue. Love that depends on physical proximity perishes in absence; but love founded upon spiritual reverence transcends all separation.'

'True, O King!' cried the Vetala, and flew back to his tree.
moral: A bond forged in shared virtue cannot be severed by oceans, exile, or death.
